verdicts.rationale: The API check found no API or developer page (radix.com/api returns 404), and the vendor describes integrations and data connectivity only as future work (c5).
verdicts.missing: Any public API documentation, developer page or statement that an API exists for reading or changing deals, models or rent rolls.

verdicts.rationale: Nothing in the pack mentions an MCP server for Radix Underwriting.
verdicts.missing: Any official MCP server, announcement or setup steps.

verdicts.rationale: The pack shows no CLI, SDK, code samples, package-registry listing or public repository from the vendor.
verdicts.missing: Any vendor-maintained CLI or SDK on a public registry or repository, or even code samples.

verdicts.rationale: No webhooks or event subscriptions are shown, and the checks found no API or developer documentation that could offer them.
verdicts.missing: Any documented webhooks, event subscriptions or third-party automation triggers; na does not apply because customers upload and change their own deal data.

verdicts.rationale: With no API shown, the pack shows no API keys, OAuth clients or credential scopes.
verdicts.missing: Any API keys, OAuth clients, or documented scopes, roles or permissions for agent credentials; na does not apply because no credential-free API is shown.

verdicts.rationale: No OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL or other machine-readable spec is shown, and no API was found.
verdicts.missing: Any machine-readable API specification, public or behind login.

verdicts.rationale: The help center redirects to a login page (c9) and no public documentation was found, so there is no llms.txt file or Markdown documentation.
verdicts.missing: Any public documentation, llms.txt file or Markdown versions of documentation pages.

verdicts.rationale: The pack shows no sandbox, test mode or developer environment, whether self-serve or on request.
verdicts.missing: Any sandbox, test mode or developer environment; na does not apply because there is no read-only published-data API.

verdicts.rationale: The Radix Underwriting product page mentions 'Excel-ready exports' (c4), but the pack shows no documentation of what can be exported or whether it can be done in bulk.
verdicts.missing: Documentation of a self-serve bulk export, which records it covers and its formats; help docs are behind a login, and the PDF/Excel export in c7 belongs to the separate Radix Intelligence comps product.

verdicts.rationale: Every call to action on the product page is Get a Demo or Log In (c6), with no self-serve sign-up or free trial shown.
verdicts.missing: Any self-serve sign-up, paid-plan checkout or free trial without a sales call.

verdicts.rationale: No pricing page exists (radix.com/pricing returns 404) and the product page offers only Get a Demo (c6).
verdicts.missing: Any published prices, starting price or plan fees.

verdicts.rationale: No API is shown, so there is no evidence that deals can be created, read or moved between stages programmatically.
verdicts.missing: API documentation for creating deals and updating their stage or status, or any third-party integration that does so.

verdicts.rationale: The product page says users can upload rent rolls and operating statements and get structured data back (c3, with c8 on the rent roll processor), but only through the in-app upload, since no API or upload endpoint is documented.
verdicts.missing: A documented API or upload endpoint, the structured output format, and any test of the extraction; the evidence is vendor marketing, and c8 dates from October 2025.

verdicts.rationale: The product page pairs AI-driven models and scenario testing with 'Excel-ready exports' (c4), which points to a manual in-app export of underwriting results, with no API shown.
verdicts.missing: Confirmation that exports include cash flows, returns or valuation results, documentation of the export, and any API endpoint for outputs.

verdicts.rationale: No API is shown, so there is no evidence that documents can be attached to a deal or read back programmatically.
verdicts.missing: API documentation for uploading documents to a deal and listing or downloading them; c3 describes only in-app upload of financial documents for extraction.
